product: Natural uranium U3O8 concentrate from 27 in-situ recovery deposits grouped into 14 Kazakh mining assets, plus fuel pellets and uranium products via Ulba-FA. Sold under long-term, short-term and spot contracts through Astana headquarters and Switzerland-based trader TH Kazakatom AG.
demand: Utilities are shifting from spot reliance to long-term inventory security. 38 countries pledged to triple nuclear power by 2050; the U.S. Department of Energy approved USD 17.5bn of conditional loans for ten AP1000 reactors; SMR construction started at TerraPower, Kairos and X-energy; reactor life extensions add further demand.
pricing_power: Pricing power is returning to producers with large proven reserves. 1H26 long-term price reached USD 95.50 per lb (+15.50 y/y) and spot averaged USD 85.98 (+24%); management says no price is high enough to justify higher supply. Legacy fixed-price ceilings still cap realised price at USD 64.51 per lb.
competition: Cameco, Orano, Uzbekistan's Navoiyuran, Rosatom's Uranium One, Denison Mines and Uranium Energy Corp. New ISR supply is starting in Mongolia, Uzbekistan, the United States and Canada. Russian supply plus the UK ban on Russian-origin uranium in force since 20 May 2026 are reshaping trade flows.
team: CEO Meirzhan Yussupov; Director of Investor Relations Botagoz Muldagaliyeva; an eight-member Board chaired by independent director Arman Argingazin, with Samruk-Kazyna (state) holding about 75% and a free float of roughly 25%.
market_strategy: Market-centric supply discipline: value over volume, aligning production with demand, expanding the resource base through exploration such as Kyzyltu, building the TQZ sulphuric-acid plant, and signing multi-year contracts in India, China and Russia to convert long-dated demand into committed sales.
bull: 1H26 revenue +9% on realised price USD 67.88/lb (+16%); long-term price USD 95.50/lb; management says no price justifies more supply; 2026 guidance 50.7-53.3 Mlb; EGM on China/Russia contracts due 7 Oct 2026.
bear: 1H26 net profit -9%, EBITDA -12%, operating cash flow -55%; cost of sales +14%; realised USD 64.51/lb vs ~USD 90 spot; TQZ acid plant delayed to Q3 2027-Q1 2028; 2027 Russian acid terms unresolved.
falsifier: Kazatomprom cuts 2027 production guidance below 27,500 tU (100% basis), or states Russian sulphuric-acid volumes for 2027 are not secured, on or before the 20 Nov 2026 earnings date.
web_what_changed: 1H26 (21 Aug): revenue +9% to KZT 717.8bn, net profit -9%, attributable EBITDA -12%, operating cash flow -55%; 2Q26 operations update 3 Aug; TQZ sulphuric acid plant commissioning delayed 6-12 months to Q3 2027-Q1 2028; Kyzyltu exploration licence about 10,000 tU granted 21 Sep; acid update after Russia Resolution 1158 of 12 Sep; Moody's Baa1 affirmed 9 Sep, Fitch BBB 26 Aug; EGM pending on China and Russia contracts.
web_not_known_yesterday: No company filing dated 24 or 25 Sep 2026 found. Newest primary items remain 21 Sep (Kyzyltu exploration licence and Russian sulphuric-acid suppliers confirming 2026 contractual volumes) with 25 Sep commentary that management sees no price high enough to raise supply. Nothing newly disclosed since.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Price and mix, not volume. 1H26 revenue +9% was driven by Group realised price of USD 67.88 per lb (vs 58.54, +16%); production rose 9% on a 100% basis but consolidated sales fell 1% and KAP-level sales fell 13%. Spot averaged USD 85.98 per lb (+24%) and long-term USD 95.50 per lb (+15.50 year on year).
web_suppliers: Sulphuric acid, vital for in-situ recovery, comes from Russia. Suppliers confirmed full 2026 contractual volumes despite Russia Resolution 1158 of 12 Sep 2026 revising export approvals, which runs to 31 Dec 2026; 2027 terms are under negotiation. Kazatomprom's own TQZ acid plant slipped to Q3 2027-Q1 2028. Cameco's Cigar Lake had a 12-day acid-related halt in 1H26.
web_customers: Nuclear power plant operators in Asia, Europe and the Americas, served from Astana headquarters and Swiss trading arm THK. Two major contracts await EGM approval: State Nuclear Uranium Resource Development Company (SPIC, China), delivery to Alashankou, and Uranium One (Rosatom), delivery to Siberian Chemical Plant. Terms are confidential. 2026 sales guidance is 50.7-53.3 Mlb.
web_who_loses: Cameco, Orano and other higher-cost producers lose share and pricing if Kazatomprom's low-cost ISR discipline tightens supply and locks utilities into term deals. Russian-origin uranium traders lose under the UK import ban in force 20 May 2026; Sprott-style funds lose if utilities shift from spot to inventory. Non-ISR developers need higher prices to proceed.
web_contradicting_evidence: Costs outrun revenue: cost of sales +14%, operating cash flow -55% to KZT 239.6bn, net profit -9%, attributable EBITDA -12%. KAP realised price of USD 64.51 per lb sits far below roughly USD 90 spot because legacy contracts retain fixed-price ceilings. Acid dependence on Russia is unresolved for 2027; TQZ is delayed; analysts trimmed fair values in July 2026 despite the spot rally.
web_if_management_right: Term prices hold in the mid-to-high 90s, utilities keep contracting long-dated, and built inventory (Group finished goods +23% to 21.4 Mlb) sells at higher realised prices. New China, Russia and India contracts convert; output moves toward 27,500-29,000 tU on a 100% basis; dividends continue; the shares re-rate toward the roughly USD 90 consensus.
web_if_management_wrong: Russian acid export approvals or 2027 supply volumes fail first, forcing a cut to 2027 production guidance, compounded by the TQZ delay. Tenge strength, higher finance costs and rising C1 costs keep eroding net profit and cash flow while legacy price ceilings cap realised pricing and spot stays flat; the equity de-rates below USD 68.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Cameco and other Western uranium producers gain from the same term-price signal; Kazatomprom's JV partners Rosatom and Uranium One, CGN and SPIC; conversion and enrichment players such as Orano, Urenco and Centrus; the AP1000 and SMR supply chain; Kazakh rail, logistics and sulphuric-acid suppliers; uranium ETFs and Sprott Physical Uranium Trust.
